mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month predicts weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates supply-side contraction, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to profit margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decrease of at least 0.5% in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a synchronized labor and supply downturn, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.4pp AND INDPRO < previous month - 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% from the previous month, combined with a concurrent decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (implied from GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate lower earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% for three consecutive months, coupled with a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2%, signals a low-real-rate environment that historically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased equity valuation sensitivity to growth.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% for 3 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of at least 8% from the previous month for two consecutive months signals a robust residential investment recovery, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to expectations of higher construction-related earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 8% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
